root_cause_label: Agent repeatedly installs GPU/CUDA torch (triggering massive downloads and timeouts) without recognizing the CPU-only environment constraint, and later fails to align packages between the shell /usr/local interpreter and the IPython /opt/openhands-venv interpreter; the corrected strategy (CPU-only torch + sys.path patch) arrives too late and the final execution crashes due to runtime resource limits.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wasted most of its budget on repeated GPU torch install timeouts, and when the correct CPU-only install finally succeeded, an interpreter/venv mismatch and a terminal runtime crash prevented the required model artifacts from ever being produced.
t_err_evidence: Step 4: agent runs `pip install transformers peft torch accelerate` without specifying CPU-only wheels, triggering the download of the full CUDA-enabled torch (899.7 MB) plus many NVIDIA packages; this assumption that GPU torch is appropriate (or that the environment supports it) is wrong and initiates the cascading timeout/cancel cycle that dominates the trajectory.
t_commit_evidence: Step 27: the final execution attempt `python3 download_base_model.py` is blocked by a runtime crash/restart; no model artifacts were ever saved, and the trajectory ends here with nothing recoverable.
t_surface_evidence: Step 4: `pip install transformers peft torch accelerate` returns exit code -1 immediately, the first observable failure signal; step 5 then shows the command was never even executed because a previous pip process was still running (the step 4 install had started in the background), and step 6 shows a timeout while nvidia packages are downloading.
trigger_explanation: The environment has no GPU, a restricted venv (/opt/openhands-venv) without pip, and bandwidth/timeout constraints. The agent handles this by attempting a full GPU/CUDA torch install (900+ MB + NVIDIA libraries) without first probing the environment; the correct approach was CPU-only torch from the PyTorch CPU index (which the agent eventually discovers at step 17 but only after burning ~13 steps on failed GPU install cycles).
forewarning_evidence: Step 4: exit code -1 on first pip install. Step 5: command not executed because previous pip still running (concurrent_process_conflict). Step 6: timeout while downloading CUDA packages. Step 12: IPython cell shows '/opt/openhands-venv/bin/python3: No module named pip' and 'PyTorch not installed' -- clear signal of interpreter/package mismatch. Steps 5, 11 repeat the same GPU torch install command.
